full.description: This image is a high-power light micrograph showing a histological section of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). It displays sheets of uniform, round to oval cells with hyperchromatic nuclei supported by delicate vascular or fibrous strands. The cytological features and architectural arrangement are characteristic of an endocrine neoplasm, most likely a pituitary chromophobe adenoma. The dense cellularity and regular nuclear morphology dominate the microscopic field.

random.description: This image is a high-power photomicrograph of a tissue section stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It displays a dense proliferation of undifferentiated small round blue cells with hyperchromatic nuclei. The histological appearance, characterized by sheets of uniform small round blue cells separated by a delicate vascular network, is typical of a blastemal Wilms tumor or a similar small round blue cell tumor. The classic features depicted are often used for the histopathological diagnosis of such pediatric renal neoplasms.
